observations.observation: Named credential strings and existing challenge/effect meanings work without changing generic roles.
AND requirements, OR alternatives, anonymous access and operation override follow effective source declarations; 3.0 non-OAuth scopes and 3.1 roles remain distinct.
A future kind exposing security selection must identify the selected requirement independently of author reordering; current experiment uses exact scheme-name sets.
Entry-document lookup of implicit referenced security names is an upstream-permitted policy; independent implementations of a future kind need agreement if this distinction remains observable.
Private configuration points map caller grants and credentials to named source schemes. Their observable fields would require shared interpretation only if adopted by a kind.

Conservative whole-operation exclusions, grant storage/carrier choice, staged challenges, duplicate handling, alias conflicts, budgets, cache shape and benchmark ceilings do not become generic interface mandates.
API keys remain opaque strings, including empty strings; HTTP validity and bearer grammar are checked by the client. The adapter does not predict authentication success.

promotionRule: Only demonstrated cross-implementation observable needs justify fresh minimal specification text; no automatic promotion of implementation policies.
